package.title: Web Presence: SEO, GA4, i18n Refresh

findings.title: Google Analytics Universal (analytics.js) was sunset July 2023

evidence.snippet: (see WEB-01 evidence block below; full snippet in EVIDENCE.json)

findings.impact: UA-52801750-1 is a Universal Analytics property. Google stopped processing UA hits on July 1, 2023. The site has had zero analytics collection for over 2 years. The GA snippet still loads, still sends hits, still costs bandwidth - but Google discards them on receipt.
findings.recommendation: Replace with Google Analytics 4 via gtag.js. Create a GA4 measurement ID (G-XXXXXXX) in the GA console. Update the partial. Consider adding Plausible or Fathom as a privacy-friendly alternative.

findings.title: All marketing copy is hardcoded in Ruby helper methods, not i18n

evidence.snippet:
def title_phrase
  'Denver Mobile App Development | Web Design | UX/UI Design'
end

def meta_description_content
  'Denver Mobile App Development company focused on making cutting edge apps...'
end

def meta_keywords_content
  'Denver mobile app development, Denver mobile application development, Denver mobile app developer...'
(file exists but only has the Rails default scaffolding - no vivim strings)

findings.impact: Every copy change requires editing a Ruby file, running tests, and deploying. Non-technical team members (marketers, sales) cannot edit copy. There is no path to localization. The meta_keywords_content is also a list of comma-separated SEO terms - a practice Google has ignored since 2009.
findings.recommendation: Move all user-facing strings to config/locales/en.yml under vivim: keys. Replace helper methods with t('.title') lookups. Delete the keywords meta tag entirely (Google ignores it).

findings.title: Sitemap config hardcoded to www.vivim.net

evidence.snippet:
host "www.vivim.net"

sitemap :site do
  url root_url, last_mod: Time.now, change_freq: "daily", priority: 1.0
  url mobile_url, last_mod: Time.now, change_freq: "daily", priority: 1.0
  url why_ror_url, last_mod: Time.now, change_freq: "daily", priority: 1.0
end

findings.impact: The host is hardcoded, so the sitemap cannot be regenerated for staging or a domain change without editing source. The precompiled sitemap.xml in public/sitemaps/ is committed to the repo, which means search engines see whatever was committed in 2014 unless someone manually regenerates.
findings.recommendation: Read the host from ENV. Move sitemap generation to a Rake task that runs on deploy. Add the sitemap URL to Google Search Console.

findings.title: robots.txt is fully commented out

evidence.snippet:
# See http://www.robotstxt.org/robotstxt.html for documentation...
#
# To ban all spiders from the entire site uncomment the next two lines:
# User-agent: *
# Disallow: /

findings.impact: All rules are commented out, so robots.txt is effectively empty. Search engines will crawl everything (including /up, /contact, /sitemap.xml itself). There is no reference to the sitemap, which means crawlers have to discover it via the meta tag or Search Console submission.
findings.recommendation: Uncomment User-agent: * and add an Allow: / plus a Sitemap: https://vivim.net/sitemap.xml directive. Disallow /up so the health check is not indexed.

findings.title: No canonical URL or Open Graph tags

evidence.snippet: (see WEB-05 evidence block below; full layout head section)

findings.evidenceBlock:
Original lines 1-18 of app/views/layouts/application.html.slim:

  doctype html
  html
    head
      title=title_phrase
      meta name="description" content="#{meta_description_content}"
      meta name="keywords" content="#{meta_keywords_content}"
  \tmeta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0"
  \tmeta http-equiv="X-UA-Compatible" content="IE=edge"
      link rel="shortcut icon" href="/favicon.png"
      = csrf_meta_tags
      = stylesheet_link_tag 'application', 'data-turbolinks-track' => true
      = javascript_include_tag 'application', 'data-turbolinks-track' => true
      link href='http://fonts.googleapis.com/css?family=Source+Sans+Pro...' rel='stylesheet' type='text/css'

Key markers: no rel="canonical" link tag
            no og:* meta tags
            no twitter:card meta tags
            http:// fonts URL (also flagged in WEB-07)
findings.impact: Without rel=canonical, search engines may index both www and non-www versions of the same page, splitting page rank. Without Open Graph tags, social shares (Facebook, LinkedIn, Slack) show no preview image or title.
findings.recommendation: Add canonical_link_tag to the layout. Add og:title, og:description, og:image, og:url meta tags. Add twitter:card tags for X/Twitter previews.

findings.title: No JSON-LD structured data

evidence.snippet: (no script type='application/ld+json' tag anywhere in the layout)

findings.impact: Without structured data, Google does not know the business is a local service in Denver with a phone number and address. The site misses out on Local Business rich results, which are the primary way mobile users find service businesses.
findings.recommendation: Add a LocalBusiness JSON-LD block to the layout, populated from a single config file or i18n entry. Include name, address, geo, telephone, openingHours, url, and sameAs (social profiles).

findings.title: Google Fonts loaded over HTTP (not HTTPS)
findings.impact: Loading fonts over HTTP on an HTTPS page triggers mixed-content warnings in modern browsers, and the request may be blocked entirely. Browsers also no longer cache cross-origin HTTP resources securely.
findings.recommendation: Change http:// to https://. Better yet, self-host the font subset to avoid the third-party request and improve Core Web Vitals.
